title: Rex Sacrorum — Roman Sacral Kingship Evidence Dossier
title_ru: Rex Sacrorum — досье по римскому сакральному царству

confidence_scale.A: directly attested by ancient source and/or strong epigraphic evidence
confidence_scale.B: strongly supported reconstruction; some details remain debated
confidence_scale.C: plausible scholarly interpretation or inference; not directly established
confidence_scale.D: traditional, popular, or weakly supported claim retained only as hypothesis

identity.core_characterization: sacral kingship retained without ordinary royal political and military command

core_facts.claim: Public priesthood carrying royal sacral functions; normally life tenure.
Patrician and subject to strict confarreatio requirements: born from confarreate parents and himself married by confarreatio.
Incompatible with ordinary magistracy / active civil-military command; the Dolabella affair of 180 BCE shows this in practice.
Festus preserves an archaic ritual ranking in which Rex precedes Flamen Dialis, Flamen Martialis, Flamen Quirinalis and Pontifex Maximus.
Later Republican practical authority placed the rex beneath the pontifex maximus despite archaic ritual precedence.
Recurring duties included Kalends/Nones calendar rites, Agonium sacrifice in the Regia, Regifugium and QRCF-related functions.

traditional_republican_transfer.claim: After expulsion of the kings, political/military powers passed to republican magistrates while royal sacral functions were partly retained by rex sacrorum.
traditional_republican_transfer.caveat: The foundation narratives are retrospective, not contemporary documentation.

older_rex_priest_continuity.claim: The Republican rex sacrorum may continue an older king-priest institution that already coexisted with political/military leaders, possibly from the late seventh century BCE.
older_rex_priest_continuity.archaeological_basis: The Regia sequence does not independently prove simultaneous creation of the priesthood and the Republic.

constitutional_design.later_relation_to_pontifex_maximus: practically subordinate despite older ceremonial precedence

comitia_calata.role: used for inauguration of a rex or flamines

pontifical_augural_process.claim: ancient tradition assigns pontiffs and augurs roles in choice/inauguration

ordo_sacerdotum.interpretation: ritual/ceremonial precedence, not Republican political supremacy
ordo_sacerdotum.caveat: May preserve a regal/archaic ordering rather than later Republican institutional power.

kalends.rex: sacrifice and calendrical/new-moon functions at the opening of the month
kalends.regina: sacrifice to Juno in the Regia

nones.function: announcement of feriae / festival days of the month

agonia.core_fact: rex sacrorum sacrificed in the Regia on dies agonales
agonia.janus_specificity: Ovid explicitly places Janus at the January Agonium; extant calendars do not assign a deity to Agonium, so the Janus link is strong but does not prove exclusive priesthood.

regifugium.core_fact: rite/sacrifice associated with the Comitium and a ritual-flight tradition
regifugium.ancient_historical_explanation: some ancient writers linked it to the expulsion of Tarquinius Superbus
regifugium.alternative_interpretation: symbolic ritual flight of rex sacrorum; original meaning disputed
regifugium.critical_distinction: Regifugium proper is February 24; March 24 and May 24 are QRCF days.

qrcf.core_rule: nefastus before completion of the indicated rex/comitiare act, fastus afterward

strenae.fact: laurel branches were placed at the house of rex sacrorum, as at houses of major flamines, Vesta's temple and curiae
strenae.interpretation: contextual priestly honor, not a unique rex rite

regina_sacrorum.identity: wife and ritual counterpart of rex sacrorum

kalends_rite.victim: sow or female lamb in later literary reporting

paired_structure.claim: rex and regina performed distinct but coordinated rites; the regina was not merely a passive spouse

epigraphic_attestation.name: Sergia Paullina
epigraphic_attestation.relation: regina associated with Cn. Pinarius Cornelius Severus

wife_death_resignation_claim.assessment: The resignation rule is directly documented for Flamen Dialis. Modern scholarship explicitly says we do not know whether rex sacrorum had the same rule, though analogy makes it plausible.

evidence_for: Ovid Fast. 1.317-334 places Janus at the January Agonium and then describes rex sacrorum propitiating the divine powers with a ram.
Varro independently attests rex sacrificing a ram in the Regia on dies Agonales.
The office's calendrical opening functions are contextually compatible with Janus themes of beginnings, but this is not proof of exclusive service.
evidence_limiting: OCD notes that extant calendars assign no deity to Agonium.
Ovid does not establish an institutional title 'high priest of Janus'.
The office belongs to a broader calendrical and public-sacral system, including coordinated Juno rites through the regina.
janus_connection.safe_statement_ru: Между rex sacrorum и Янусом засвидетельствована сильная ритуальная связь, особенно в январский Agonium; называть Rex Sacrorum верховным жрецом Януса как установленный факт слишком сильно.

Regia.role: major ritual locus of rex/regina sacrorum
Regia.note: architectural sequence is central to origin debate

Comitium.role: central to Regifugium and QRCF and the boundary between ritual rex and civic-political space

Lapis_Niger.fact: archaic inscriptional complex includes rex and a kalator-related term
Lapis_Niger.assessment: cannot securely identify this rex with later Republican rex sacrorum

republican.name: P. Cloelius Siculus
republican.note: later ritual-resignation tradition is textually confused and retained cautiously

failed_candidate.name: L. Cornelius Dolabella
failed_candidate.importance: shows incompatibility with duumvir navalis and authority of pontifex maximus

imperial_epigraphic.name: fragmentary rex associated with Manlia Fadilla

italic_parallels.assessment: Italic/municipal parallels illuminate the category but do not establish the exact origin of the Roman office.

late_republic.assessment: office became less prominent and could experience vacancies; continuous occupancy cannot be demonstrated for every interval

abolition_date.note: older reference works sometimes extend the office to the Christian imperial period/Theodosius; exact endpoint is not treated here as established

open_questions.question: Created only after expulsion of kings, or continuation of an older king-priest?
Was Janus the formal January Agonium recipient, and was there any exclusive Janus priesthood?
What precisely did comitiare mean in QRCF?
Did rex resign if regina died?
Which earliest named holders are historical?
Exact chronology of shift from archaic ritual primacy to pontifex-maximus supremacy?

patterns: AUTHORITY_SPLIT: coercive/political power can be separated from continuity/ritual authority.
TITLE_WITHOUT_IMPERIUM: a powerful title can preserve a function while barred from command.
THRESHOLD_CALENDAR: duties cluster around beginnings, calendar transitions and fastus/nefastus boundaries.
DUAL_ROLE_PAIR: rex and regina form coordinated but non-identical ritual roles.
MEMORY_WITHOUT_RESTORATION: sacral kingship can be retained without restoring monarchy.
RANK_NE_CONTROL: ceremonial precedence and practical administrative supremacy can belong to different offices.
janus_system_relevance.firewall: Modern comparative design analogies only; no claim that Roman priests encoded or caused the JANUS system.

negative_controls.misstatement: Rex Sacrorum was politically supreme in Republican Rome.
negative_controls.correction: Festus gives ritual precedence; later practical religious authority lay with pontifex maximus and rex lacked ordinary command.

negative_controls.misstatement: Rex Sacrorum was definitely the high priest of Janus.
negative_controls.correction: Strong Janus association exists for January Agonium, but exclusive priesthood is not established and extant calendars do not name a deity for Agonium.

negative_controls.misstatement: Regifugium occurred on February, March and May 24.
negative_controls.correction: Regifugium proper is February 24; March 24 and May 24 are QRCF.

negative_controls.misstatement: If Regina Sacrorum died, Rex certainly had to resign.
negative_controls.correction: Directly attested for Flamen Dialis, not for rex sacrorum; Rex case is inference by analogy.

negative_controls.misstatement: The office was unquestionably invented in 509 BCE.
negative_controls.correction: That is the traditional transfer model; archaeology permits an older king-priest continuity model.

negative_controls.misstatement: Lapis Niger proves Republican rex sacrorum existed in the monarchy.
negative_controls.correction: The archaic rex reference is important but its identity is ambiguous.

summary_ru.bottom_line: Rex Sacrorum — устойчивый институт, сохранявший сакральную сторону царского титула при отделении от обычной политико-военной власти.
summary_ru.strongest_janus_link: Январский Agonium у Овидия прямо вводится через Януса, а rex sacrorum выполняет связанный жертвенный обряд; это сильная ассоциация, но не доказательство эксклюзивного жречества Януса.
summary_ru.strongest_structural_link_for_janus_syst: Римская система исторически демонстрирует разделение титула/ритуальной непрерывности и командной власти.
